events.title: First Friday: Summer Chill
events.description:
Grab a friend and start the weekend with art, music, and culture in the Grand Center Arts District. This classic summer lineup—cold drinks and specialty cocktails, yard games outside in our courtyard, and chill vibes—is the perfect evening to share with friends. Enjoy free samples of Ted Drewes frozen custard, a sweet treat which will be on the new menu at the CAM café starting on July 8!

Registration is encouraged; click here to sign up. Please contact programs@camstl.org with any questions.

events.title: Family Day
events.description:
Join us for our annual summer Family Day at the Contemporary Art Museum St. Louis! This free, drop-in event celebrates creativity, connection, and community. Families are invited to enjoy an engaging morning of live jazz performances by HEAL Center for the Arts, a puppet meet and greet with St. Louis Shakespeare Festival, and a scavenger hunt with Pulitzer Arts Foundation. We’ll have free snacks from Selma’s Treats, sodas and seltzers compliments of 2nd Shift Brewing, and free samples of frozen custard from Ted Drewes—now available at the CAM Café!

Outside, explore the YMCA mobile game bus, yard games in the courtyard, as well as activities and resources courtesy of Freddie Ford Family Foundation and Washington University St. Louis’ Office for Socially Engaged Practice.

Beyond CAM’s Family Day event, families are invited to spend the morning exploring more arts experiences throughout the Grand Center Arts District. At neighboring institutions like the Sheldon Concert Hall and Art Galleries, families can enjoy free face painting and hands-on activities. St. Louis Public Radio will also be set up in the Public Media Commons, where families can record a radio greeting or testimonial that might end up on air and get a temporary tattoo. Kids In The Arts District will be hosting a free musical performance by Marko Polo at The Listening Room @ High Low. Pick up a Grand Center Family Day BINGO card to guide your adventure through the district and earn free swag.

Registration is encouraged; click here to sign up. Please contact programs@camstl.org with any questions.

Schedule

  • 10:00 am: Doors open; activities begin
  • 10:30 am: Performance by HEAL Center for the Arts
  • 11:30 am: Puppet show by St. Louis Shakespeare Festival
  • 12:30 pm: Performance by HEAL Center for the Arts

events.title: CAM Connect: The Wisdom Exchange
events.description:
The Wisdom Exchange, a new series created by Bluebird Society, is a monthly lunch gathering for LGBTQ+ community members to come together around the shared experience of aging—exchanging knowledge, planning ahead, and strengthening the networks of chosen families. Kick off the series at CAM, where the Alzheimer’s Association will lead an engaging session on brain health and cognitive wellness. Enjoy a light lunch, take part in hands-on activities led by Alexis Creamer, CAM Community Access Manager, and connect with your community, whether you’re reuniting with old friends or making new ones. 

This program is offered as part of CAM Connect, a series of programs designed to foster accessibility and social connection through art in collaboration with organizations serving North St. Louis residents, older adults, and people with disabilities.

Doors open at 10:45 am.

Please click here to sign up.

events.title: Feast Your Eyes: Andrew Cisneros
events.description:
Enjoy a unique dining experience at Feast Your Eyes, a delicious way to enjoy the culinary and visual arts. This event features acclaimed chef Andrew Cisneros, owner of contemporary Peruvian bistro jalea. and Brasas chicken shop, who will serve a special three-course dinner with refined yet approachable dishes inspired by the exhibitions on view at CAM. Delight your senses with this one-of-a-kind event! 

Tickets are priced at $125 for CAM members; $150 for non-members and include a special cocktail or mocktail, along with an open bar throughout the evening. Two seating times at 5:15 pm (sold out!) and 7:45 pm. Space is limited. 

A few tickets remain. Click here to purchase.

CAM members should have received an email with the discount code. Please contact us at members@camstl.org or 314.535.0770 x 204 with any questions or to renew your membership. 

Accessibility Notes

Feast Your Eyes includes a three-course dinner with a specialty cocktail or mocktail along with an open bar. The menu will be peanut-free and will include a vegetarian option upon request. Ticket holders will be contacted in advance to confirm any dietary restrictions.

About Andrew Cisneros

Andrew Cisneros began his culinary journey in high school, competing in cooking competitions as a member of Francis Howell North’s culinary team. After graduating from L’Ecole Culinaire, Cisneros trained at the Saint Louis Club under Chef Pierre Chambrin, former White House chef, where he built a strong foundation in classical French techniques that continue to shape his culinary philosophy.

He went on to further hone his craft at several acclaimed establishments, including Elaia under Ben Poremba, Privado + Público with Mike Randolph, Dia’s Room at the Four Seasons under Gerard Craft, as well as Salt at the Ritz-Carlton Amelia Island and TPC Sawgrass during the Players Championship.

events.title: First Friday: Season Wrap Party
events.description:
Grab a friend and start your weekend with art, music, and culture in the Grand Center Arts District. 

This First Friday is a chance to get a last look at our spring/summer exhibitions before they close for the season on August 9. As always, enjoy extended gallery hours for some late night browsing, and drinks will be available for purchase.

Join DJ $ol for an evening made for music lovers and music philosophers, including a special edition of her beloved listening club, Is It A Classic?. For this edition, Lady Gaga’s album Born This Way will be played front to back as the room collectively decides whether it has earned classic status. $ol selected this album to trace a through line of self-determination from Gaga’s songwriting to the stories unfolding across CAM’s galleries. Reserve a seat for the full listening session and debate, or drop by anytime to tune into an exhibition-inspired playlist and weigh in on the night’s musical question via our community message board.

Also, stop by a station hosted by Brick City Photography Center to create a free cyanotype and talk photography!

Schedule

  • 5:00 pm: Bar opens; Brick City Photography Center photo station and Community Message Board open
  • 6:00 pm: Is It A Classic? listening session

Registration for a seat at the table for Is It A Classic? is sold out.

Attendance to the galleries, Brick City Photography Center photo station, listening area, and message board are free and open to the public.

About DJ $ol and Is It A Classic?

Raised in Oakland, California, and based in St. Louis, $ol is a multidisciplinary artist, DJ, and cultural conductor whose work centers art, dialogue, and connection. In 2021, she founded Is It A Classic? (IIAC), St. Louis’s only listening club dedicated to music philosophy and spirited debate. The idea emerged from a personal practice of listening to albums alone and asking a simple question: does this hold up as a classic? As the series’ first guest and ongoing host, $ol has transformed that curiosity into a public forum where music enthusiasts gather to explore influential albums, cultural impact, and the evolving nature of artistic legacy.

Through IIAC and other creative projects, $ol creates accessible spaces where conversation becomes a tool for learning and community building. Her work is rooted in a belief that shared cultural experiences can foster meaningful connection, creating ease around intimacy and encouraging strangers to engage with one another in authentic ways.

About Brick City Photography Center

Brick City Photography Center is a St. Louis nonprofit dedicated to preserving and advancing the art of analog, darkroom-based photography. Founded by longtime photographer and educator Jeff Sass, the center grew out of a lifelong passion for teaching chemical photography to students of all ages. Brick City offers community members access to darkroom space, equipment, and hands-on instruction, championing traditional and alternative photographic processes as vital, living art forms in an increasingly digital world.

events.title: Artist Talk + Tour in The Ville: Tony Cokes
events.description:
Please note: the start and end location for this event is Counterpublic’s Hub in The Ville at 4140 Dr. Martin Luther King Drive, St. Louis, MO 63113

In celebration of his exhibition at CAM as a part of Counterpublic 2026: Coyote Time, join artist Tony Cokes and Counterpublic curator Stefanie Hessler for a conversation at Antioch Baptist Church as part of a walking tour of The Ville neighborhood. The talk and tour will trace the full arc of Cokes’s project, which includes a video on CAM’s facade for Street Views, a video installed in the church, and billboards bridging these two sites. Counterpublic staff and artists will also take visitors to other Counterpublic 2026 artists work in the neighborhood. Comfortable shoes and weather appropriate clothing is recommended. The tour route requires navigating uneven and unreliable city sidewalks. Please note that this event takes place in The Ville and coincides with the Northside Trap Run.

Visit Counterpublic for event details and to register.

 

About the artist

Tony Cokes (b. 1956, Richmond, VA) lives and works in Providence, Rhode Island, where he serves as Professor in the Department of Modern Culture and Media at Brown University. Cokes was awarded a MacArthur Foundation Fellowship in 2024 and the Rome Prize in 2022–23. A solo presentation of his work, Texts, Tracks, Talks (1992-2026), will open at The Institute of Contemporary Art at Virginia Commonwealth University, on September 18, 2026. Other recent solo exhibitions include Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein, Vaduz (2025–26); Batalha Centro de Cinema, Porto (2024–25); Dia Bridgehampton, The Dan Flavin Art Institute, Bridgehampton, New York (2023–24); Hessel Museum of Art, Annandale-on-Hudson, New York (2024); and many others.

events.title: Great Rivers Biennial 2026 Artist + Juror Panel Discussion
events.description:
Celebrate the 12th edition of the Great Rivers Biennial (GRB) in this panel conversation with GRB artists Vaughn Terrell Davis Jr., Lauren dela Roche, and Vincent Stemmler and jurors Leslie Hewitt, Margot Norton, and Pavel Pyś. Ferring Foundation Chief Curator Dean Daderko moderates the discussion.

Registration is encouraged; please click here to sign up. 

Members at the Sustainer level and above, email members@camstl.org to request reserved seating.

Accessibility notes

  • To request an American Sign Language (ASL) interpreter for this event, please contact programs@camstl.org with as much prior notice possible to ensure availability.

 

About the Artists

Vaughn Terrell Davis Jr. (b. 1995, St. Louis, MO) has exhibited work at Romer Young Gallery, San Francisco; Nazarian / Curcio, Los Angeles; Dimensions Variable, Miami; The Luminary, St. Louis; and Tripoli Gallery, Wainscott, NY, among others. In 2023, Davis created a torn flag sculpture to be hoisted outdoors at Laumeier Sculpture Park in Sappington, MO, in tandem with his solo exhibition in the museum’s gallery. Davis is an exhibiting artist for Counterpublic 2026: Coyote Time, and holds a BFA in Sculpture from Webster University in St. Louis. 

Lauren dela Roche (b. 1983, Santa Rosa, CA) is the recipient of several grants and residencies, including a 2024 Joan Mitchell Center residency in New Orleans. Dela Roche is represented by Eric Firestone Gallery in New York. Her work is found in the collections of the Minneapolis Institute of Art, the North Dakota Museum of Art, and the Hessel Museum of Art at Bard College, among others. She has resided in the Midwest since young adulthood and currently lives and works near St. Louis. 

Vincent Stemmler’s (b. 1989, St. Louis, MO) most recent solo exhibition, Doom Scroll, was presented by the Kranzberg Arts Foundation, St. Louis in 2023. That same year, he was featured in Counterpublic, St. Louis’s citywide public art triennial. Stemmler holds a BFA from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago and an MFA from Southern Illinois University Edwardsville, with a record of exhibitions spanning local, national, and international venues.

About the Jurors

Working with photography, sculpture, and site-specific installations, Leslie Hewitt addresses fluid notions of time. Oscillating between the illusionary potential of photography and the physical weight of sculpture, her compositions  suggest the porosity between intimate and sociopolitical lives. A selection of recent and forthcoming exhibitions include the Museum of Modern Art in New York; the Studio Museum in Harlem; Artists Space in New York; Project Row Houses in Houston; and LA > < ART in Los Angeles. Hewitt has held residencies at the Studio Museum in Harlem, the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, the Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University and the American Academy in Berlin, Germany amongst others. In 2012, CAM presented a solo exhibition of her work, Sudden Glare of the Sun.

Margot Norton is Chief Curator at the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive (BAMPFA), where she leads the curatorial team and oversees the exhibition program. At BAMPFA she curated and co-curated MATRIX 283/ Gabriel Chaile (2023); MATRIX 286/Amol K. Patil (through April 2025); To Exalt the Ephemeral: The (Im)permanent Collection (through July 2025); and the BAMPFA presentation of Making Their Mark: Works from the Shah Garg Collection (through April 2025). She regularly contributes to exhibition catalogues and publications and is also co-founder and current editorial council member of Museums Moving Forward, an independent, limited-life organization devoted to envisioning and creating a more just museum sector by 2030. She holds an MA in Curatorial Studies from Columbia University, New York. 

Pavel Pyś is the Curator of Visual Arts and Collections Strategy at the Walker Art Center. At the Walker, he has curated solo exhibitions by Daniel Buren, Paul Chan, Pan Daijing, Michaela Eichwald, Christine Sun Kim, Carolyn Lazard, Ralph Lemon & Kevin Beasley, Sarah Michelson, and Elizabeth Price, as well as the group exhibition The Body Electric (2019). In 2018, he was awarded an Andy Warhol Foundation Curatorial Fellowship which aided research towards Multiple Realities: Experimental Art from the Eastern Bloc, 1960s-80s, presented at the Walker, Phoenix Art Museum and Vancouver Art Gallery. Pyś is closely involved in leading the strategic vision, development, and long-range planning of the Walker’s collection. In 2025, he was awarded a Center for Curatorial Leadership Fellowship. Pyś received an MFA in Curating from Goldsmiths College in 2010 and an MSc in Culture & Society from the London School of Economics in 2009.

events.title: Sparkle #8 / A Performance by Ayana Evans
events.description:
In conjunction with her exhibition Nobody’s Gonna Love You the Way I Do, Ayana Evans presents a newly commissioned live performance that brings her distinctive unapologetic, emotionally invigorating, and deeply improvisatory practice to attendees. 

Sparkle #8 unfolds in CAM’s Performance Space among Evans’s exhibition, welcoming audiences to interact directly with Evans. During these performances, Evans typically assigns both individual and collective tasks that turn audience members from viewers to participants, and which speak to relevant and pressing concerns. Evans’s performances are vehicles through which she challenges the ways class, race, gender, and sex are implicated in prevailing sociopolitical attitudes.

events.title: C.R.E.A.M. Fair
events.description:
In conjunction with her exhibition Nobody’s Gonna Love You the Way I Do, Ayana Evans brings her ongoing community engagement project C.R.E.A.M. (Cash Rules Everything Around Me) to St. Louis. Part block party and part opportunity fair, C.R.E.A.M. connects community members—such as students, job seekers, queer activists, artists, and people affected by the justice system—with free resources and supportive services. Whether you, someone you love, or members of your community are looking for helpful paths forward, come to the C.R.E.A.M. Fair for a joyful communal space centered on care, creativity, and collective support. Bright, comfortable clothes are encouraged—no suits allowed!

Schedule

  • Meet with admissions representatives from Harris-Stowe State University, Ranken Technical College, and Webster University

Spend an evening experiencing connections between opera and the visual arts with the musical program series “Artwork and Arias,” presented by CAM and Opera Theatre of Saint Louis (OTSL). Curated by OTSL Gerdine Young Artist Edmond Rodriguez, this iteration explores the power of unapologetic voices, from the operatic stage to museum galleries to the street. Rodriguez’s selections and voice put forward an opportunity for vulnerability to become a shared experience of healing, speaking one’s truth, and building the world we want to live in.

About the Artists

Tenor Edmond Rodriguez is a 2026 Gerdine Young Artist at Opera Theatre of Saint Louis, where he recently sang the Waiter in The Light in the Piazza and the Young Collector in A Streetcar Named Desire. He holds a master’s degree in voice at Rice University’s Shepherd School of Music. Recent engagements include a 2025 debut with Lang Lang and the Chicago Symphony Orchestra at the Ravinia Music Festival, and a world premiere of The House on Mango Street at the Glimmerglass Festival. Edmond has been a featured soloist with the Los Angeles Philharmonic and Los Angeles Master Chorale. He is an active session singer in the Los Angeles film and television industries, with credits including Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker,  Encanto, Nope, Wicked. 

Jonathan Heaney is a pianist and vocal coach based in St. Louis, Missouri. He frequently collaborates with Opera Theatre of Saint Louis, most recently serving as Associate Music Director for Joshua’s Boots. Upcoming engagements include serving as Repetiteur for Cinderella and A Little Night Music during OTSL’s 2027 Festival Season. He also performs regularly with Union Avenue Opera and Winter Opera St. Louis. Heaney’s previous professional affiliations included The Juilliard School, Manhattan School of Music, On Site Opera, Seagle Festival, and Brevard Music Center. He holds a bachelor’s degree in piano performance from Washington University in St. Louis and a master’s degree in vocal accompaniment from Manhattan School of Music.

events.title: First Friday: Celebrating Lauren dela Roche
events.description:
Enjoy art, music, and culture in the Grand Center Arts District on the first Friday of the month. This event celebrates Great Rivers Biennial 2026 artist Lauren dela Roche. Drop in and make watercolor paintings on found paper, echoing dela Roche’s materials and process, while enjoying light bites and a live music set from Jane Wave.

Schedule

  • 5:00 pm Doors open / Bar opens
  • 6:00–8:30 pm Music by Jane Wave and drop-in art activity

Registration is encouraged; please here to register.

About the Artists

Lauren dela Roche (b. 1983, Santa Rosa, CA) is a self-described queer punk feminist artist whose autodidactic approach integrates a broad range of references, including zines, European modernisms, and autobiography. Though largely self-taught, her consumption of visual culture and art history allows her to draw upon long artistic traditions, remixing diverse sources ranging from Egon Schiele’s line work and transgressive cinema to Persian miniatures, Greek mythology, and folklore. Dela Roche’s recent work—painted on found, mended, and repurposed cotton feed sacks—shows multiplying, echoing views of a nude woman, a recurring central character. In her iconic, fresh style, her work ties deeply to the land, agriculture, ecology, and systems of caretaking. For nearly a decade, dela Roche lived off the grid in Northern Minnesota, building a cabin from found materials and becoming fully self-reliant through farming. She is the recipient of several grants and residencies, including a 2024 Joan Mitchell Center residency in New Orleans. Dela Roche is represented by Eric Firestone Gallery in New York. Her work is found in the collections of the Minneapolis Institute of Art, the North Dakota Museum of Art, and the Hessel Museum of Art at Bard College, among others. She has resided in the Midwest since young adulthood and currently lives and works near St. Louis.

Jane Wave is the solo experimental project of Sam Pounders, a self-taught sound artist based in St. Louis, Missouri. Producing songs in a home studio, Jane Wave experiments with vocals, bass-heavy pop rhythms, found sounds and instrument loops. Weaving traditional music, primitive punk, no wave and abstract sound, Wave’s performances are coordinated and improvised. Wave has performed for the last 10 years in the St. Louis area, both as a solo musician and as a member in bands such as Swear Beam, Fried E.M. and Pineapple RnR. Her recent album, Quality Time is available for streaming on Subvert FM and Bandcamp; a tape release is forthcoming in late 2026.

events.title: Gallery Talk and Film Screening: Every Line Becomes a Circle
events.description:
CAM is pleased to partner with the 35th Annual Whitaker St. Louis International Film Festival to present a gallery talk and film screening event that explores the world of contemporary art through a cinematic lens. In collaboration with the Goethe-Institut St. Louis, the event explores connections between CAM’s current exhibitions with new releases that are part of the Festival’s fine arts spotlight. 

This year’s screening event celebrates the importance of artistic expression to creative aging. Following a welcome reception, scholar Dr. Brian D. Carpenter and film director/producer Lynnette Luis will engage in a gallery talk with CAM’s Director of Learning and Engagement Michelle Dezember about Juanita McNeely‘s epic Triskaidekaptych (1986), creative aging, and the value of artistic practice and appreciation for health resilience and wellbeing. The evening continues with a screening of Every Line Becomes a Circle, a documentary following 93-year-old German artist Inge Besgen’s decades-long persistence to find herself in post-war Germany and become an artist in her 50s despite many setbacks. Taken together, the evening explores how life’s experiences—especially memory, pain, and reckoning—take on deeper significance and power when explored through painting and abstraction.

This event is free and open to the public. Complimentary food is provided, and drinks are available for purchase.

Schedule

  • 6:30 pm: Doors open for gallery viewing and welcome reception
  • 7:00 pm: Gallery Talk
  • 7:40 pm: Film Screening
  • 8:30 pm: Q&A with producer/director Lynnette Luis

Accessibility notes

  • Seating is first come, first served and set up in tables and chairs. If you require seating, please email programs@camstl.org to reserve a seat.
  • To request an American Sign Language (ASL) interpreter for this event, please contact programs@camstl.org with as much prior notice possible to ensure availability.
  • The film is in German with English subtitles.
  • Please note that food and drink is not allowed in the galleries, but is welcome in the screening area.

About the speakers

Brian D. Carpenter, PhD is Professor of Psychological & Brain Sciences​ and Co-Director, Harvey A. Friedman Center for Aging at Washington University in St. Louis. Professor Carpenter conducts research on the clinical psychology of aging. His research focuses on family relationships in late life, with a particular emphasis on collaborative family communication and decision-making.

Lynnette Luis is a director/producer from California, now based in Berlin. She entered the film industry in 1994 with an internship at Paramount and has worked in editing and production for Disney and German TV. She trained at the Koelner Filmhaus and has extensive experience as an assistant director and script supervisor. She directed and produced Every Line Becomes A Circle.

About the film

Every Line Becomes A Circle is a powerful documentary about 93-year-old German artist Inge Besgen. Her life and art reflect how every experience and choice shapes who we become. Inge’s story is one of resilience, creativity, and the belief that it’s never too late to follow your dreams.

Every Line Becomes A Circle (2024), directed by Lynnette Luis, Christopher Leete, and Ottilie Maters. 50 minutes.

events.title: Talk: Jane Panetta on Juanita McNeely
events.description:
Join Jane Panetta, Aaron I. Fleischman Curator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, for a conversation with CAM Ferring Foundation Chief Curator Dean Daderko as they trace the artistic journey around the monumental painting Triskaidekaptych, the centerpiece of CAM’s exhibition of work by Juanita McNeely as part of Counterpublic 2026: Coyote Time. The conversation will expand to include Simon Kelly, Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at the Saint Louis Art Museum (SLAM) to offer insight into the simultaneous presentation at SLAM and the complementary first-ever solo presentations of McNeely’s work in her hometown.

Jane Panetta is the Aaron I. Fleischman Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Panetta joined The Met in 2023, where she’s ushered in major acquisitions, recently curating The Genesis Facade Commission: Jeffrey Gibson, The Animal That Therefore I Am (2025), and David Hartt: Peripheries (2026). Additionally, Panetta is working closely on the museum’s forthcoming Tang Wing for Modern and Contemporary Art. Previously, Panetta served as the Nancy and Fred Poses Curator and Director of the Collection at the Whitney Museum of American Art, where she oversaw acquisitions (including work by Juanita McNeely), collection displays, and co-direction of long-term planning for the collection. At the Whitney, she served on the curatorial team for America Is Hard to See (2015), co-curated the 2019 Whitney Biennial, and organized solo presentations of the work of Njideka Akunyili Crosby, Willa Nasatir, Juan Antonio Olivares, Jennifer Packer, and Rose B. Simpson. Prior to this, she worked at The Museum of Modern Art on monographic exhibitions including Edvard Munch: The Modern Life of the Soul (2006), Richard Serra: Forty Years (2007), and James Ensor (2009). Panetta received her B.A. from Haverford College and her M.A. in Art History from Hunter College and serves on the Madison Square Park Conservancy’s Public Art Consortium.

events.title: Day With(out) Art Film Screenings
events.description:
Gather in dialogue, creative expression, and community building for Day With(out) Art. Starting at 10:00 am, a selection of short video works commissioned by Visual AIDS will be presented on a loop at CAM for drop-in viewing in a dedicated screening space until 7:00 pm. At 5:00 pm, a culminating event features a community conversation, a special screening, and a response wall to gather reflections about the films and HIV/AIDS. A portion of the AIDS Memorial quilt will also be on view. 

Day With(out) Art is a national program that originated in 1989 on World AIDS Day as a celebration of the lives and achievements of lost artists and colleagues. With participation from hundreds of organizations, Day With(out) Art encourages ongoing efforts to de-stigmatize and find a cure for HIV by showing care for those living with a positive status. 

Schedule

  • 5:00 pm Galleries open; complimentary snacks and drinks available for purchase
  • 5:30 pm Welcome comments from Lawrence Hudson-Lewis (Director of Prevention, Project ARK) and screening of seeds in a dying colony
  • 6:30 pm Q&A

Video Synopses

Edgar Hudson Mdendu, There is an Elephant in the Room (Tanzania)

A young person flees home after a life-altering discovery, carrying the weight of things that cannot be said out loud. He encounters an activist fighting to be heard and a care worker sustaining others through daily acts of survival. Through dance and movement, the film offers a quiet story of survival, exile, and return, asking what it takes to face the elephant that everyone knows is there.

Bruna Kury and Matheus Mello, Viral Borders: Geopolitics of a Pandemic (Brazil/Spain)

A visual manifesto that transforms the HIV virus into a mirror of empire, where data, propaganda, and flesh collide. Through a frenetic digital collage, the film exposes the biopolitical machinery that controls the body and weaponizes borders against life itself.

Sido Lansari, Forevermore (Morocco/France)

Forevermore weaves together archival echoes, poetic fragments, and testimonies of Arab queer lives touched by HIV, spanning generations and geographies. Through the voices of the dead and the living, the film transforms silenced histories into a collective act of remembrance and resistance.

Micaela Cyrino, How to project your voice without causing an earthquake (Brazil)

Carolina lives alone in an apartment on the outskirts of São Paulo. Every morning she faces the city’s frenetic pace during the long commute from her home to work. In her thoughts, her grandmother’s wisdom always returns; in her headphones, it’s always the same rap. In her bag, she carries the book of recipes, baths, and blessings she inherited from her grandmother and the desire to end the day well.

Response Wall 

The response wall provides prompts for reflection and conversation around the videos and broader conversations of HIV/AIDS. Questions include:

  • How are some people’s health and lives protected while others are ignored? How do artists make this visible?
  • What do traditions offer to people facing hardship or stigma?
  • These artists come from Tanzania, Brazil, Spain, Morocco, and France–what do you know or want to know about experiences from our community in St. Louis?
